meta.purpose: Structured, append-only record of every review cycle run via the review-harness skill. Schema and procedure shared across review-api/review-web/review-infra/review-harness — see .claude/skills/review-shared/PROCEDURE.md.
howToUse: Append a new entry: status 'requested' if just logging pending work, or 'reviewing' if starting both passes immediately.
Move through fixing -> re_reviewing -> awaiting_merge_approval as the cycle progresses.
Never set 'merged' yourself unless a human has confirmed the merge actually happened — this skill never runs `gh pr merge`.

statusLegend.requested: Pending work identified/logged, cycle not yet actively started.
statusLegend.re_reviewing: Fixes pushed, re-verifying against the real remote branch.
statusLegend.awaiting_merge_approval: Cycle complete, PR ready, waiting on a human to merge.
statusLegend.no_issues_found: Both passes ran, genuinely nothing to report.

meta.invariantsRef: review-shared/PROCEDURE.md + this domain's own internal-consistency checks (see SKILL.md).

features.title: PR #23 — devops-request-grant skill + graph automation (retroactively logged)
features.description: This review cycle happened informally, before this skill existed — logged retroactively as the real precedent this skill's procedure was written from, not a fabricated example. /code-review (high) found 5 issues (4 real bugs, 1 acknowledged tradeoff); fixed 4, pushed. A second /code-review (medium) pass re-flagged 2 already-fixed items — root-caused to the review fork checking stale local working-tree duplicates instead of the real pushed branch (a genuine harness-review lesson, now written into review-shared/PROCEDURE.md step 8 explicitly).
acceptance: Fixes verified against the real remote branch via GitHub API, not local state (done after the stale-state issue surfaced).
PR merged only after explicit human instruction each step of the way.
verify: gh api repos/.../contents/.claude/skills/devops-request-grant/cleanup.sh?ref=... confirmed the -t 0 fix was genuinely live before merge
features.rubric: PASS overall. Dimension 2 (real re-verification) is the standout lesson: the second review pass's false re-flags were only caught because fixes were independently re-checked against the real GitHub content rather than trusted at face value — exactly the discipline review-shared/evaluator-rubric.md's dimension 2 now codifies.

features.title: PR #24 — the four review skills' own introduction (dogfooded on itself)
features.description: review-harness's scope explicitly covers .claude/skills/** — PR #24 is exactly that, so this is the skill reviewing the PR that created it. First review attempt accidentally targeted the wrong local branch (same class of mistake as PR #23's second pass, now doubly-confirmed as a real recurring risk, not a one-off); corrected by fetching the PR's actual diff directly via `gh pr diff 24` before dispatching a review against that file. Found 3 real issues: the seeded review-web entry's 'requested' status wasn't in the documented enum, clean-state-checklist.md's merge gate contradicted PROCEDURE.md's own documented merged-confirmation flow, and the loop no-op guard omitted awaiting_merge_approval as a terminal state.
acceptance: /code-review-equivalent pass ran against the PR's actual fetched diff, not an ambiguous local checkout.
All 3 findings fixed and verified against the real remote branch via GitHub API before being reported as resolved.
PR not merged by this skill — stopped at awaiting_merge_approval per explicit human decision.
verify: gh api repos/.../contents/.claude/skills/review-shared/PROCEDURE.md?ref=feat/domain-review-skills -- confirmed 'requested' and awaiting_merge_approval fixes genuinely live
gh pr view 24 --json state -> OPEN (not merged by this cycle)
features.rubric: PASS. Dimension 2 (real re-verification against the actual target, not local state) was directly load-bearing here too: the first review attempt's misdirected result was only caught by checking git diff --stat main...HEAD against the diff's own stated content and noticing the mismatch, not by trusting the returned findings at face value.
